claims.text: The additively manufactured Al0.2Co1.5CrFeNi1.5Ti0.3 alloy has an fcc matrix.
The starting alloy is homogeneous apart from minor microsegregation introduced by additive manufacturing.
The starting alloy has minimal preexisting oxide formation and stable mechanical properties.
Microsegregated regions in the alloy are enriched in Al and Ti, particularly along grain boundaries.
Elevated-temperature oxidizing exposure causes localized oxidation at Al- and Ti-rich microsegregated regions.
Localized oxidation produces brittle intergranular oxide precipitates.
Growth of brittle oxides along grain boundaries deteriorates intergranular bonding.
Loss of intergranular cohesion causes microcrack formation and ultimately catastrophic failure.
Higher oxygen partial pressure will produce thicker and more continuous grain-boundary oxides.
Higher oxygen partial pressure will cause earlier embrittlement and lower fracture toughness relative to the starting-state baseline.
Reducing atmospheres will suppress or delay oxide formation relative to oxidizing atmospheres.
Suppression or delay of oxide-scale formation under reducing conditions will alter or delay the degradation pathway.
Mechanical integrity will decline under reducing exposure despite less pronounced oxide formation.
Eventual failure is expected during reducing exposure at 600–800 °C.
The proposed degradation mechanism applies to distinctly oxidizing or reducing exposures between approximately 600 and 800 °C.
